windows.note: English-family TCG products enumerated from Yugipedia set pages (all five English release-date properties) joined with the YGOPRODeck bulk dump; see data/imported/releases-report.json for known gaps.

Japanese OCG products and promotional distributions from the beginning of the OCG (per Yugipedia's own "Series 1" window, 1999-02-01) through the day before the August 26, 1999 Tokyo Dome event, hand-curated (curated:true) from Yugipedia's Series 1 set/product/card pages and cross-verified against the "Series 1 sets" navigation template for completeness. 20 products certified; 5 anomalies discovered during research are accounted for in data/releases/gaps.json (gap-ocg1999-*), none unresolved. The December 16, 1998 Duel Monsters (video game 1) collector's cards are deliberately excluded: Yugipedia's own Series 1 sets template classifies them, and the entire Bandai Carddass/Sealdass card lines, as "Non-OCG (1997-1999)", predating the OCG's actual 1999-02 launch.

known_gaps: 4 products have no printings (no YGOPRODeck card lists them; mostly repackagings and non-card products)
8 in-window cards could not be matched to BabelCDB
62 products where YGOPRODeck's date matches no Yugipedia date (recorded in the report; Yugipedia governs)
34 Yugipedia-dated in-window products matched no YGOPRODeck set and are absent (no printing rosters available)
4 printings carry numbers from a different product's prefix (upstream set-membership quirks; validator warns per case)
Renamed products (Magic Ruler / Spell Ruler) import as two products sharing dates

ocg-jp 1999: the Duel Monsters National Tournament prize cards' top-placer tier, the Tokyo Dome invitation Ticket cards, and 3 small redundant promo distributions (V Jump August 1999 Special Present, V Jump Festa 1999, the DM2 trial-meeting card) are accounted for by resolved-safe gap-ocg1999-* records rather than product rosters; see data/releases/gaps.json.
notes: known_gaps above are importer-detected anomaly tallies kept for bookkeeping, NOT unresolved certification failures: certification is governed by the gap ledger (data/releases/gaps.json), and the validator requires every anomaly counted here to be accounted for by a ledger record (unaccounted anomalies fail validation as gaps.unaccounted).
